A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TwELL/hybrid sparse-LLM study. Their main text, algorithms, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison; v2's final page continues an existing appendix paragraph.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendices C–D report original model-training experiments, downstream accuracy, kernel efficiency measurements and activation-sparsity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the original training, downstream evaluation, efficiency and sparsity-analysis results in Section 4 and Appendices C–D.

M1.justification: The TwELL/hybrid formats, L1 objective and inference/training procedures are unchanged. Corrected row/column descriptions agree with Algorithm 2 and Equation (3) already present in v1; restored code-listing text does not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same fineweb-edu training corpus and seven downstream benchmarks: ARC-Easy/Challenge, HellaSwag, OpenBookQA, PIQA, WinoGrande and CommonsenseQA. No evaluated dataset or task scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The evaluated dense baselines and activation/architecture comparisons in Tables 1 and 3–5 are unchanged. The newly cited Macko work is discussed only as related research, not evaluated as a comparator.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix B retain the model sizes, training budgets, context lengths, batch settings, hardware and evaluation metrics. The new batched-GEMM discussion describes the existing setting rather than changing the evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The L1 sweeps, activation and gating ablations, dead-neuron mitigation experiments, layer/token analyses and RTX6000 comparison are retained unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices C–D.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged throughout the empirical sections and appendices. v2 adds no seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: The numerical results and plotted findings in Tables 1 and 3–6 and Figures 2–12 are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains the 2B model's reported 20.5% forward-execution and 21.9% training speedups.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(6) and the mathematical reasoning are retained. Section 3.1 corrects variable/index typos without substantively revising definitions, assumptions or derivations; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution list and concluding discussion retain the same claims about sparse kernels, over 99% sparsity with negligible performance impact, and throughput, energy and memory benefits.

C2.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E.1 newly explain the focus on compute-bound GEMM with thousands of input tokens, distinguishing it from prior memory-bound GEMV for single/few-token processing. This clarifies applicability and why the setting supports both training and inference benefits.

D1.justification: Appendix A, Listings 1–3 restore statements previously truncated at percent signs, including PTX operands, register settings, lane-index expressions and divisibility assertions. This improves implementation documentation; it does not establish changed experimental settings or kernels.

R1.justification: v2 adds Macko and Boža (2025) and sharpens research positioning through the GEMV/GEMM distinction in Section 5 and Appendix E.1. It also removes the blanket 'structured' characterization of prior post-training sparsity. Q-Sparse remains in Appendix E despite its omission from Section 5.

P1.justification: Changes comprise localized wording and matrix-index/row-column corrections, rewritten related-work passages, updated date text and added acknowledgments. The main narrative and section/appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1–12 and Tables 1–6 retain their designs and contents. Appendix A's code display and syntax highlighting are repaired, while acknowledgments and reference/text reflow produce limited layout changes, including moving Appendix E's final paragraph to page 48.

improvement.justification: v2 improves technical usability by restoring truncated CUDA statements and correcting misleading matrix descriptions. The clarified GEMM/GEMV distinction also makes the contribution's scope easier to assess. These are useful, limited improvements; the method and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
